Question Choices: Fill: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One alternate interior angle measures $82^\circ$. What is the measure of the other alternate interior angle?
Hints: Alternate interior angles are strictly equal
Solution: Alternate interior angles on opposite sides of the transversal are equal when the lines are parallel. Therefore the other angle is 82°.

Question Choices: Fill: In a triangle, two angles measure $55^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. Find the third angle in degrees.
Hints: All three angles must add up to 180 degrees
Solution: Triangle angles total 180°. The third is 180−(55+75)=50°. Checking the sum recovers 180°.

Question Choices: Fill: An angle formed by a transversal and a parallel line measures $115^\circ$. Find its supplementary acute angle.
Hints: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees
Solution: The requested pair is supplementary, so x+115=180°. Thus x=65°.

Question Choices: Fill: If $(7x - 5)^\circ$ and $(5x + 9)^\circ$ are vertical angles, find $x$.
Hints: Vertical angles are equal to each other
Solution: Vertical angles are equal: (7 × x - 5)=(5 × x + 9). Collect variable terms and solve to get x=7. Substitution gives 44° in BOTH expressions, so the equality checks.

Question Choices: Fill: An equilateral triangle has all angles equal. One angle is written as $(3x + 15)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.
Hints: Each angle in an equilateral triangle is exactly 60 degrees
Solution: Each equilateral-triangle angle is 180÷3=60°. Solve (3 × x + 15)=60 to get x=15. Substitution gives 60°.
